newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Ryanair opens Irish telemarketing centre.
newsitem.headline: Ryanair opens Irish telemarketing centre.

text.p: Irish enterprise and employment minister Richard Bruton on Wednesday opened Ryanair Direct, a telemarketing centre established by private Irish airline Ryanair.
The 2.5 million punt central reservation and telemarketing centre was supported by industrial development agency Forbairt and employs 110 people at present.
With further growth and new routes, Ryanair expects this figure to rise to 200 before December 1997.

"The establishment of this new international telemarketing centre will reduce waiting time for customers, therefore making Ryanair's low fares even more accessible to customers, travel agents and the general public," Ryanair said in a statement.
The centre is the largest telemarketing operation established by an Irish company in Ireland and is expected to deal with up to five million calls in 1997.
Ireland has become the leading European location for teleservices centres servicing overseas markets in recent years.
Employment in Irish-based internationally traded teleservices has growth from just over 500 in 1990 to more than 3,000.
